label: Pipelined traversals
mechanism: the host syncs inside a traversal are deleted (device-side page-table lookup + prefill readbacks deferred past the decode step), so a step's prefill and decode traversals occupy different GPUs of the layer-split pipeline at the same time
hypothesis: The engine shards the 66 layers into four contiguous per-device segments (server.build_resident: 'layer split [16, 17, 16, 17] over 4 GPUs'), so ONE traversal is a serial walk across four GPUs and idles three of them. That has been true for the whole Stage-3 trajectory and is visible without instrumentation: sampling nvidia-smi at 0.4 s during the WORKER's own canonical bench of exp-0017 gives a marching 96/0/0/0 -> 0/99/0/0 -> 0/0/100/0 -> 0/0/0/95 wave (/workspace/logs/t_pipeline_bubble_exp0018_util.log). What pinned it there is host synchronisation, not data dependency: every device->host sync inside a traversal blocks the host until THAT device catches up, so the next traversal cannot be handed to the GPUs. The prefill traversal had 23 — kv.PagedKV._flat_slots does a .tolist() on the page table for append and again for gather on each of the 11 global layers (the sync exp-0005 flagged and which the batched decode core already routes around), plus the closing int(lg.argmax()). ONE mechanism removes them: _flat_slots indexes the device mirror of the page table (table_dev_row, which ensure_pages already maintains for the batched decode core — value-identical integers; the non-pooled batch-1 path is untouched), and Engine.prefill/prefill_batch split into an enqueue half returning the fp32 logits rows still on device plus a readback half, with Scheduler.step enqueueing the step's prefill groups, then the decode traversal, and only then reading the prefill tokens back. This step's admissions are excluded from the decode traversal by construction (admit_step == step_count) and walk disjoint pool slots, so nothing depends on the tokens being held. Both original entry points survive as the enqueue+readback composition, so every caller outside the scheduler is unchanged. NOTHING NUMERIC MOVES — identical kernels, identical shapes, identical per-sequence op order, only when the host hands work over — and the arms say exactly that: serial vs pipelined token streams are EXACTLY EQUAL (not envelope-close) over 14 sequences / 56 tokens, two identical pipelined runs are bitwise equal (the t_b3-adapted determinism arm), and the D13 teacher-forced gate is GREEN and bit-identical to the accepted exp-0016/0015b/0017 numbers (parity_pass true, agree 379/400 = 0.9475, delta_mean 0.043856 vs bar 0.054281, delta_max 0.396472). Measured on GPUs 4-7 with one resident load, 8 residents plus a cohort of 6 at ISL 690-800, warm-up pinned to the same 1024 key-length bucket so no graph capture lands in a timed arm (engine/pyengine/tests/t_pipeline_prefill.py, log /workspace/logs/t_pipeline_prefill_exp0018_out.log): the MIXED step — the only step shape with two traversals to overlap — goes 1.409 s -> 1.373 s = 1.026x (36 ms), while prefill-only and decode-only steps are unchanged (1.593/1.539 and 0.168/0.168) as they must be. Kill switch PYENGINE_PIPELINE_PREFILL=0.
predicted_delta: +0.5 to +1.5% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s: ~224.2 vs the best same-protocol accepted row 221.8 (merge bar 222.5). This is deliberately a THIN prediction and the cycle model behind it is stated so it can be falsified: the measured pieces reproduce exp-0017's accepted row to within 2% (1083 reqs at cohort 6 = ~180 prefill traversals x 1.373 s = 247 s, plus 2166 decode steps x 0.168 s = 364 s, total 611 s vs the row's 625 s), and the measured 36 ms applies only to the ~180 mixed steps = 6.5 s of the box. Floor case: if the server's admission pattern yields fewer mixed steps than the cohort model predicts, the saving shrinks toward zero and the row lands at ~221.8 — a rejection that still fixes the 23 per-traversal syncs and prices the pipeline bubble. The ceiling is 3 x decode_stage ~= 126 ms per mixed step (a perfectly pipelined pair costs 4 prefill segments + 1 decode segment instead of 4 + 4); only 36 ms was realized, and the residual is on device 0, where the decode step's first segment AND the eager layer-2 island (graphrun._run_island, the one region exp-0012 could not capture) sit on the very device the prefill occupies first. That is the ranked-next attack and it is sized in experiments/EXP0018_RECORD.md: fold layer 2's bf16 experts into the captured graph (it unblocks this ceiling AND removes ~400 M~1-2-row launches from a 364 s decode term), then microbatched decode, which is the only way a layer-split model gets more than two independent traversals to overlap — and which needs exactly the sync-free traversal this experiment builds.
